rice-county-guide.label: Rice County clinic guide and dates

prep.label: Event
prep.text: Use the organizer’s current listing. The venue can change.

prep.label: Parts
prep.text: The organizer keeps a limited supply of spare parts.

prep.label: Check-in
prep.text: Regular events use drop-in check-in. Expect a waiver and an item intake form.

prep.label: Item count
prep.text: The organizer asks visitors to bring no more than two items each. Check the specific event for its item categories.

prep.label: Check-in
prep.text: Sign up on arrival. Intake closes one hour before the event ends.

prep.label: Item count
prep.text: During busy periods, volunteers examine one item per person.

prep.label: Parts
prep.text: The visitor guide says the café currently cannot supply replacement parts.

prep.label: Check-in
prep.text: York Region residents can register ahead for an appointment. The operator lists registration by event.

prep.label: Parts
prep.text: Bring any replacement part you already know the item needs.

prep.label: Check-in
prep.text: Visitors are seen in arrival order. Sign the repair form and plan to stay with your item.

prep.label: Item count
prep.text: When the event is busy, one item per person is examined. Late arrivals may be turned away in the final hour.

prep.label: Parts
prep.text: Visitors pay separately for any new materials used.

prep.label: Item count
prep.text: Bring up to two items you can carry in. The county excludes oversized items.

prep.label: Event
prep.text: Use the current county listing for the clinic venue and date.

prep.label: Check-in
prep.text: Check in on arrival. A volunteer gives you a time slot after intake, in arrival order. Advance booking is unavailable.

prep.label: Size
prep.text: Bring an item one person can carry. The council describes a 30-minute repair slot.

rules.text: The café excludes bicycle repairs and points to local bike shops and the public library’s rotating bicycle clinic.
The visitor FAQ lists bicycles. Check the event listing for its repair categories.
The visitor guide lists bikes among volunteer skills. Check which fixers will be at your event.
The program lists bicycles, subject to volunteers at the specific event.
Many local cafés decline adult bicycle repairs. Ask the local organizer what they can do.
The council lists bicycle repair among its event categories.
The café lists microwaves among its exclusions.
The program names microwaves among small appliances it can consider, depending on available fixers.
The network’s house rules exclude microwave repairs.
The council excludes microwaves from the electronics category.
The FAQ says many toasters are unsuitable for repair. Confirm your item first.
The visitor FAQ asks people to leave toasters at home.
The county names toasters as items its clinics may be able to repair.
The council lists toasters among items it will not assess.
The café excludes phone repairs. The FAQ mentions advice on use.
The visitor FAQ asks people to leave phones at home.
The council lists phone diagnostics and help with setup, storage and updates. Ask about physical repairs before going.
The program rules exclude electrical e-bike issues. The program lists mechanical issues separately.
The FAQ excludes clothing and curtain alterations.
The visitor guide says clothing volunteers focus on mending. Ask before bringing an alteration.
The program excludes hems and alterations. It lists small tears and clothing repairs separately.
Many local cafés decline clothing alterations. Ask the host for its policy.
The county lists clothing and other soft goods for mending or alterations. Ask about the specific alteration you want.
The council excludes clothing alterations and separately lists clean textiles and clothing for repairs.
